draft.title: Pedigrees and sex-linked traits
card: A pedigree chart traces a trait through a family. Squares show males, circles show females, and shaded shapes show people who have the trait.
A line between a square and a circle joins two parents. Lines below them lead to their children.
Sex-linked genes sit on the X chromosome. Females have two X chromosomes (XX) and males have one X and one Y (XY).

A male has only one X, so a single recessive allele on it shows as the trait. A female needs the recessive allele on both X chromosomes. This is why red-green colour blindness is seen more often in males.
A son gets his X from his mother and his Y from his father.
draft.remember: A male has one X, so one recessive allele on it shows. A female needs two.

a.q: Which statement best explains how an X-linked recessive trait comes to show more often in males?
opts: Males have one X, so one recessive allele shows
Males have two X chromosomes, so the allele is doubled
Females have a Y chromosome that hides the allele
The gene sits on the Y chromosome, which only males have
a.why: A male has only one X chromosome, so there is no second allele to mask a recessive one. A female has two X chromosomes, so she needs the recessive allele on both. The gene is on the X, not the Y.
a.clue: Think about how many X chromosomes each sex has.

b.q: In a pedigree, a shaded square has a shaded circle as his partner. Their son is not shaded, and the trait is sex-linked recessive on the X. Which statement is correct?
opts: This cannot happen, as the mother passes on her only allele
This is likely, as the son gets his father's X chromosome
The son must have got a Y chromosome from his mother
The father passed the allele on to his son on the Y
b.why: A shaded mother has the recessive allele on both X chromosomes, so she passes one to every son. A son gets his X from his mother and his Y from his father. A son with the trait would be expected, so an unshaded son cannot happen.
b.clue: A son gets his X from one parent only. Which one?

a.best: Males have one X, so one recessive allele shows

b.best: This cannot happen, as the mother passes on her only allele

problems.detail: The stem states as fact that the son is not shaded, then the right answer says this cannot happen. Presenting an impossible situation as a given is confusing. It would be clearer to ask whether an unshaded son is possible.

'Her only allele' is misleading. The card says a female has two X chromosomes, so she has two alleles for this gene. A clearer version would be 'as every X the mother can pass on carries the recessive allele'.
